qa.q: What is a full contour zirconia crown?
a: A full contour zirconia crown, also called a monolithic zirconia crown, is milled from one solid piece of zirconia with no porcelain layered on top. At our zirconia dental lab, we design full contour zirconia dental crowns digitally, mill them on Roland equipment, sinter them and finish each one by hand.

qa.q: How long do full contour zirconia crowns take?
a: Our RX form lists them at 7 in-lab working days, for 1 to 3 units and for 4 or more. Call the lab about cases of 8 units or more. Weekends, holidays and shipping time aren’t counted.

qa.q: Should I choose full contour or layered zirconia?
a: Full contour zirconia suits back teeth where strength comes first, since there’s no layered porcelain to chip. Layered zirconia gives the ceramist more control over translucency on front teeth. Compare both on our layered porcelain crowns page.

qa.q: Can I send a digital scan?
a: Yes. Tick “Digital imp scan” on the RX form. We accept scans from iTero, Trios and similar systems. Contact the lab to confirm how to send the files.

qa.q: How do I tell the lab the shade?
a: Write the shade, and the stump shade where relevant, on the RX form. For shade-critical cases, tick “Custom Shade”, then email photos to photos@dentalconceptssf.com or book a custom shade appointment on (415) 558-9717.

qa.q: Is anything extra needed for anterior cases?
a: Yes. Our RX form asks for a pre-op or study model with every anterior case, along with the shade and stump shade.

qa.q: What does the warranty cover?
a: If a placed final fixed restoration fails within one year, we repair or replace it with no charge for materials and workmanship once it’s returned to us (restrictions apply). We also guarantee the fit to the die or cast model, provided the tooth was reduced to the manufacturer’s recommendations.

close.sub: Call 1-800-700-LABS or email the team before you send patient records, and we’ll confirm the best way to get the case to us.

qa.q: What are layered porcelain dental crowns?
a: Layered porcelain crowns have porcelain built up by hand, in layers, over a milled zirconia core. They’re also called porcelain-fused-to-zirconia (PFZ) crowns, and they appear as “Zirconia (Layered)” on our RX form.

qa.q: When should I prescribe a layered porcelain crown?
a: They’re a common choice for front teeth, single centrals and other shade-critical cases, where translucency and surface character matter most. For molars in patients who clench or grind, full contour zirconia is often the safer pick.

qa.q: How long do layered porcelain crowns take?
a: Our RX form lists layered zirconia at 10 in-lab working days for 1 to 3 units and for 4 or more. An esthetic crown with a custom shade appointment takes 15 days, as does a single central when the patient attends the shade visit promptly.

qa.q: Can my patient visit the lab for shade matching?
a: Yes. Tick “Custom Shade” on the RX form and call (415) 558-9717 to book an appointment at 244 9th Street. Visits take about 15 to 20 minutes.

qa.q: Is anything extra needed for anterior cases?
a: Yes. Our RX form asks for a pre-op or study model with every anterior case, along with the shade and stump shade.

qa.q: Can I send a digital scan?
a: Yes. Tick “Digital imp scan” on the RX form. We accept scans from iTero, Trios and similar systems. Contact the lab to confirm how to send the files.

qa.q: Can I rush a layered porcelain crown?
a: Rush service is available on most products for up to 4 units, when you pre-schedule it on (415) 558-9716. Cases needed within 7 business days carry a $100 per unit surcharge.

close.sub: Call 1-800-700-LABS or email the team before you send patient records, and we’ll confirm the best way to get the case to us.

qa.q: Is E.max the same as lithium disilicate?
a: E.max is the name many dentists use for lithium disilicate, a strong glass ceramic. Our RX form lists it as “Lithium Disilicate”, and our E.max dental lab work covers veneers, inlays, onlays and crowns.

qa.q: Which restorations can you make in lithium disilicate?
a: Veneers, inlays, onlays and crowns. Note which one you need on the RX form, along with the shade and stump shade.

qa.q: Why does the RX form ask for a stump shade?
a: Lithium disilicate is translucent, so the color of the prepared tooth can show through the restoration. Knowing the stump shade lets the technician plan for it.

qa.q: How long do E.max crowns take?

qa.q: What is a screw-retained implant crown?
a: A screw-retained implant crown is screwed onto the implant, so the clinician can remove it later if needed. Our screw-retained implant crown lab supplies it lab cemented as one piece with a screw access hole, or as a separate crown and abutment.

qa.q: What’s the difference between lab cemented and two pieces?
a: Lab cemented (one piece with a hole) means we bond the crown to its abutment here, and you screw the unit into place through the access hole. Uncemented (two pieces) means the crown and abutment arrive separately.

qa.q: How long do implant crowns take?
a: Our RX form lists implant crowns and abutments at 15 in-lab working days for 1 to 3 units, and implant cases at 3 to 4 weeks in total. Call the lab about 4 or more units.

qa.q: Can the screw access be angled?
a: Our RX form has an option for angulated screw access, where it’s possible. It depends on the implant system and position, so we’ll confirm it for your case.

qa.q: What do digital implant cases need?
a: A full arch gingival scan taken without the healing abutment, as our RX form notes, plus the implant system and size. Tick “Digital imp scan” and contact the lab to confirm how to send the files.

qa.q: Can the lab supply the implant parts?
a: Yes. Tick “Lab to provide parts” on the RX form and write in the implant system and size.

qa.q: How do I tell the lab the shade?
a: Write the shade, and the stump shade where relevant, on the RX form. For shade-critical cases, tick “Custom Shade”, then email photos to photos@dentalconceptssf.com or book a custom shade appointment on (415) 558-9717.

qa.q: Why choose an implant crown dental lab that also makes the abutment?
a: When one lab designs the crown and the abutment together, the fit, emergence and screw access are planned as one restoration. See our custom abutments page for material options.

close.sub: Call 1-800-700-LABS or email the team before you send patient records, and we’ll confirm the best way to get the case to us.
